bib.title: Distilling Step-by-Step! Outperforming Larger Language Models with Less Training Data and Smaller Model Sizes

question: Can rationales extracted from an LLM serve as extra supervision so that small task-specific models need less training data and fewer parameters to match or beat the LLM?
hypothesis: Rationales contain task knowledge that is hard to infer from inputs alone, so predicting them as an auxiliary task improves label prediction in small models.
contributions: Distilling step-by-step: multi-task training of a small model on labels plus LLM-extracted rationales
Better performance than finetuning and distillation with over 50% fewer training examples on average (up to over 85%)
Smaller models outperform 540B PaLM few-shot CoT (up to 2000x smaller)
Ablations on teacher size and multi-task vs single-task

method.summary: Few-shot CoT prompts 540B PaLM to produce a label and rationale for each input. A pretrained T5 is then trained multi-task with task prefixes [label] and [rationale], loss L = L_label + lambda L_rationale. Only the label is generated at test time.
method.task: task-specific distillation / finetuning with LLM rationales (NLI, commonsense QA, math word problems)

datasets.name: CQA (CommonsenseQA with cos-e explanations)
datasets.split: original validation set used as test set because test labels unavailable

datasets.name: ASDiv
datasets.split: used as extra unlabeled augmentation for SVAMP

training.objective: L = L_label + lambda L_rationale (cross-entropy on label and rationale tokens), multi-task via task prefixes
training.seeds: 4 random runs, standard error in plots

other.lambda: value of lambda in Eq. 3 not stated
other.unlabeled setting: standard task distillation uses PaLM predicted labels as targets

inference.prompting: few-shot CoT (about 10-shot per task) following Wei et al. 2022 where available, own examples for new datasets; each prompt is a triplet (x_p, r_p, y_p)

other.test-time: student predicts label only; no rationale or LLM needed

eval.protocol: 4 random runs; 220M T5-Base for data-reduction and ablation experiments; 100% data for model-size experiments

results.claim: A 770M T5 beats few-shot PaLM-540B on ANLI with 80% of the labeled data, while standard finetuning cannot match it with 100%
results.quote: our finetuned 770M T5 model outperforms the few-shot prompted 540B PaLM model using only 80% of available data on a benchmark

results.claim: On e-SNLI, 12.5% of labeled data with Distilling step-by-step beats standard finetuning on 100%
results.quote: by using only 12.5% of the full e-SNLI dataset

results.claim: Examples reduction needed to outperform standard finetuning on ANLI
results.quote: we achieve 75%, 25%, and 20% reduction in training examples required to out-perform standard finetuning on ANLI, CQA, and SVAMP respectively
results.note: Quote in text reads 'out-perform' hyphenated across line; CQA 25%, SVAMP 20%.

results.claim: On e-SNLI a 220M T5 outperforms PaLM few-shot CoT with only 0.1% of the dataset
On ANLI, Distilling step-by-step beats standard finetuning and distillation across T5 sizes by an average
results.quote: outperforms standard finetuning and distillation by an average of 8% and 13% on task accuracy

results.claim: Unlabeled setting: 11B T5 beats PaLM few-shot CoT with less than 3% of PaLM size
results.quote: by using 11B T5 with less than 3% of PaLM’s size

limits: Needs about 10-shot human-written CoT demonstrations per task
Slight training-time compute overhead for rationale generation
LLM reasoning is limited on complex reasoning and planning tasks (Valmeekam 2022); effect of rationale quality left to future work
Only 4 datasets, 3 task types; accuracy results mostly shown in figures (not tabulated)
Optimizer, lambda, schedule, warmup, decoding settings not stated
